pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly see the tour as a front-loaded tour of the interface and replace it with a guided first invoice, naming the steps to cut or defer. pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers see the tour as an inventory of the interface, build the fix around sending a first invoice and name the steps to cut. A is more coherent. Its suggested check, drop-off at steps 2–4, says little about the 80% who leave at step 1, though its no-tour control is a good idea. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers diagnose the tour as a feature inventory, cut steps 2–4 and 7 by name, defer the bank connection and replace the tour with a real first-invoice task. samples.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A fits on one screen and labels each stage right on the curve. Its jar row and rubber-band tip make it practical for a first-timer, and it gives no hour figures, saying only that time depends on the kitchen. Some of A's stage captions (Rise, Collapse) cross the curve slightly. B's diagram is cleaner, its hours are clearly marked as an example and it shows the mix window well, but the page runs past one screen and the stage cards are cut off. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B fits on one screen. pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A's diagram labels every stage, including Feed, directly in the chart. It places 'Best time to mix dough' at the peak and uses no hour counts at all ('Hours, not minutes', 'Many hours later'), so it never risks false precision. B has a clear hour axis and a caveat about temperature and feeding ratio, but its stage cards still give hour ranges. B's curve also has an odd uptick at the end, and the '1 · Fed' and 'sinks' labels crowd the line. A has one small flaw of its own: its collapse caption slightly overlaps the curve. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both pages pair a clear rise-and-fall SVG with stage labels drawn on the diagram and four stage cards, in a restrained dark palette. pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B states the key idea plainly in a 'Why timing matters' callout. It treats times as approximate, noting that warm or cool kitchens and bigger feeds change the timing and that many starters peak around 4–8 hours. A's diagram is clean, but it puts fixed hour marks on the axis and in the cards ('Peak ≈ hour 6', 'Hour 7 onward') without saying they depend on temperature. It also never spells out why the timing matters as clearly. Both have small label-and-curve overlaps: A's 'dome sinks, gets sour' and B's 'gets sour and weak', plus B's cut-off-looking 'stirred in,' label. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A states the key idea most clearly. The 'Best time to mix' box sits right on the peak, a 'Why timing matters' callout follows, and it frames timing as depending on temperature and feed size ('around 4 to 8 hours'), with a few minor label collisions (a cut-off 'stirred in,' and red text crossing the curve). B is attractive, with jar icons and shaded stage bands, but it puts exact hours on the axis and in each stage card ('Peak ≈ hour 6', 'Hour 7 onward') as if they apply to every kitchen. Its stage labels also don't line up well with their bands ('3 Peak' sits after the peak point), and the 'dome sinks' label crosses the curve.
